errors.location: Section III, equations (3)–(4), and the claim following equation (3)
errors.description: The stated unitary-waveform model does not provide the claimed T-fold SINR gain. A unitary matrix has rows of unit norm, so correlating the received signal with a row preserves that symbol’s energy; with orthogonal rows, equation (4) isolates each symbol as h_n x_{b,n}. A T-fold gain would require different energy normalization. The same equations do not show coherent combining of N antennas for each independent data symbol, so they do not establish the claimed beamforming-equivalent link-budget gain.
errors.evidence: “If the matrix F_b is unitary, the data symbols x_{b,n} can be recovered without crosstalk by the matched filters f_{b,n}† that provide the T-fold improvement of SINR”; later: “There is no loss in link budget gain compared to spatial beamforming at the transmitter.”

errors.location: Section III, equation (3), and the first numerical example
errors.description: T is used as the dimension of the T×T matrix F_b, so it must be an integer. The first numerical example sets T=18.375, which cannot instantiate the stated finite-dimensional matrix model. No alternative continuous-time definition of F_b is provided to connect that example to the model.
errors.evidence: “F_b ∈ C^{T × T}” followed by “we set T = 18.375.”

errors.location: Final summary bullet beginning “Peak data rate”
errors.description: For a fixed finite number of spatial streams, spatial multiplexing can multiply the number of streams, but it does not make rate grow linearly with SNR in general: the rate remains logarithmic in SNR at high SNR. The manuscript’s own equation (9) gives log₂(1+SNR); its linear approximation applies only at low SNR and is not a benefit specific to spatial multiplexing.
errors.evidence: “Peak data rate can be made to grow linearly with SNR by means of spatial multiplexing”; equation (9) states R = log₂(1 + SNR), and equation (10) labels the linear relation as a low-SNR approximation.

errors.location: Final summary bullet beginning “Diversity is fully exploited”
errors.description: Omnidirectional transmission can make multipath signals available, but it does not by itself ensure that spatial or temporal diversity is fully exploited. That requires independent channel observations and a receiver or coding method that combines them; the cited reasoning establishes only that propagation paths are not excluded by transmit beam direction.
errors.evidence: “Temporal and spatial diversity is fully exploited as the transmit signal is sent omni-directionally, allowing for multi-path propagation without angular restrictions.”
